_meta.description: Works whose printed head falls inside a row, so carve_cgpg_volume.py (which moves whole rows) cannot serve them. Applied by scripts/split_carved_row.py.

volumes.basis: The Euthalian apparatus Migne prints in the Oecumenius volume's front matter. Three pieces carry their own Greek head and a named author, Euthalius the Deacon, and all three heads fall mid-row, which is why the volume's pass-1 carve left them in the residual and the residual note recorded them as waiting on a splitter. Offsets read from the rows themselves on 2026-08-08 and asserted at run time against the head string and the text before it.

works.title: Prologus in epistulas Pauli
works.evidence: Head at 163:526, verbatim ΕΥΘΑΛΙΟΥ ΔΙΑΚΟΝΟΥ ΠΡΟΛΟΓΟΣ, followed by Παῦλος ὁ ἀπόστολος, Ἐβραῖος μὲν ἦν τὸ γένος. Runs to 165:82, where the Apodemiai head begins; the sentence before that cut, ὡς ἐν συντόμῳ εἰπεῖν, αὗται·, introduces the list, so it closes the prologue rather than opening the list.

works.title: Apodemiae Pauli
works.evidence: Head at 165:82. Our OCR reads it ΛΠΩΝΙΜΙΑΙ ΠΑΥΛΟΥ ΤΟΥ ΑΗΟΣΤΟΣΩν for ΑΠΟΔΗΜΙΑΙ ΠΑΥΛΟΥ ΤΟΥ ΑΠΟΣΤΟΛΟΥ; the anchor is quoted as printed here, not corrected, so the check tests the row that is actually cut. What follows is the itinerary itself, Ἀπὸ Δαμασκοῦ ἤρξατο, καὶ ἀνῆλθεν εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ. Ends at 167:2302 where the Martyrion head begins.

works.title: Martyrium Pauli
works.evidence: Head at 167:2302, ΜΑΡΤΥΡΙΟΝ ΠΑΥΛΟΥ ΤΟΥ ΑΠΟΣΤΟΑΟΥ, followed by Ἐπὶ Νέρωνος τοῦ Καίσαρος Ῥωμαίων, ἐμαρτύρησεν αὐτόθι Παῦλος. Runs to the end of 167, the last row of the block.

volumes.basis:
Gregory Palamas' Homologia and the confined archbishops' Anaphora to Anna Palaiologina, identified in 6c3a9e3 from Migne's printed titles at columns 764 and 768 (Internet Archive item patrologia.graeca.org, _151.zip, scan pages 377 and 379) and left uncarved because every seam falls inside a row. Two of the four seams sit in rows an earlier pass already moved into work files, so this cuts across three files at once.

Locus 389 is the hard one and the reason this tool takes a list of parts rather than a range: Migne's page prints the tome's metropolitan subscriptions down the left column, the Homologia's head and opening at the bottom of that column, the tome's imperial subscription in the upper right, and the Homologia's continuation at the bottom right. Our OCR read the columns in that physical order, so the row holds Homologia text at 1207-1392 AND at 3068-end with 1,676 characters of the tome in between. Joining the two gives ...Μονὰς ἐν Τριάδι, καὶ Τριὰς ἐν Μονάδι ἀσυγχύτως ἑνουμένη, καὶ ἀμερίστως διαιρουμένῃ..., which is what column 764 prints. The ΟΜΟΛΟΓΙΑ head itself the OCR dropped; the anchor is the Greek that follows it.

works.title: Confessio fidei
works.evidence: Migne prints ΟΜΟΛΟΓΙΑ ΤΗΣ ΟΡΘΟΔΟΞΟΥ ΠΙΣΤΕΩΣ, ΕΚΤΕΘΕΙΣΑ ΠΑΡΑ ΤΟΥ ΙΕΡΩΤΑΤΟΥ ΜΗΤΡΟΠΟΛΙΤΟΥ ΘΕΣΣΑΛΟΝΙΚΗΣ ΚΥΡΙΟΥ ΓΡΗΓΟΡΙΟΥ ΠΑΛΑΜΑ at column 764, so the attribution is the edition's own, the same standard that filed the encomium under Philotheus. Ends at ζωὴν τοῦ μέλλοντος ἄληκτον αἰῶνος. Ἀμήν, verified against column 768C.

works.title: Anaphora archiereorum ad Annam Palaeologinam
works.evidence: Head ΑΝΑΦΟΡΑ ΤΩΝ ΑΡΧΙΕΡΕΩΝ πρὸς τὴν κρατίστην καὶ ἁγίαν ἡμῶν κυρίαν καὶ δέσποιναν κυρίαν Ἄνναν τὴν Παλαιολογίναν survives in our own bytes at 391:3841 (column 768). The report of the confined bishops is a collective document with no single author, so it is filed under a collective label the way the synodal tomes in this volume are.

volumes.basis:
Theophylact Simocatta's block of Constantine VII's Excerpta de legationibus, the seventh and last historian in that Migne block. The other six were carved in pass 5 and displaced to corpus_secondary as witnesses of their served works on containment 0.833-0.941. Theophylact was held back at 0.697, below the 0.7 demotion gate, and the record answered the rank question and then left the block in the volume file, which answered a different question: whether to DEMOTE it, not whether it can be CARVED. It can. Its own head survives mid-row at 475:436, ΕΚ ΤΗΣ ΙΣΤΟΡΙΑΣ ΘΕΟΦΥΑΑΚΤΟΥ ΑΠΟΕΠΑΡΧΟΥ ΚΑΙ ΑΝΤΗΡΑΦΕΩΣ, that is ἐκ τῆς ἱστορίας Θεοφυλάκτου ἀπὸ ἐπάρχων καὶ ἀντιγραφέως, his own style, and the 436 characters before it are the tail of Menander's block (0.764 against the served Menander, 0.236 against the Historiae).

Rank is NOT reopened here: it stays primary, which is what pass 5 decided and what the text is already served as, so this carve changes citability and nothing else. But the number the decision rested on was measured over the block INCLUDING Menander's tail. Measured over the block alone it is 0.717, which clears the same gate rather than falling under it. Per row it is bimodal: 480-487 run 0.750-0.903 while 477, 478 and 479 sit at 0.501, 0.592 and 0.513, so the block is not uniformly the served text and the codified gate is a per-row shed rule anyway. Recorded rather than acted on; demoting it is the same entry with rank secondary and would take 4,782 tokens out of the published primary corpus, which is cisco's call.

works.title: Excerpta de legationibus
works.evidence: Head at 475:436 read from our own bytes. The block ends at 487, which closes on a complete sentence (οἱ Βάρβαροι.); 488 opens mid-sentence into Constantine's own closing proem and its containment against the Historiae falls from 0.750 to 0.218, so the boundary is sharp without a head. No TLG anchor: the Canon's tlg3130.X01/X02 for these Excerpta carry no TLG number and no word count, so nothing can be claimed (the precedent for a named author with no anchor is hierocles-grammaticus.synecdemus).

volumes.basis:
Migne PG 3 prints Pseudo-Dionysius alternating with Georgius Pachymeres' paraphrase and the switch usually falls inside a printed page. Boundaries are the volume's own display heads: from data/pg003_heads.json where the aligned table has them, and from our own bytes where our OCR kept the head (data/pg003_blocks.json). Every offset was read from data/corpus/cogPG.PG003.jsonl, never from the Internet Archive text.
The paraphrase is one work with 40 discontinuous parts: Migne numbers it PARAPHRASIS PACHYMERAE (1) to (60) continuously across the four treatises it accompanies, with no title page per treatise. It stops at (60) on the last chapter of the Mystical Theology; PG 3 prints no paraphrase of the Epistles and says so at col. 1064 (Vide Schol. S. Maximi et Paraphr. Pachym. in Epistola 1, tom. II), so loci 540-567 are Dionysius entire.
Two of those four switches are now in data/pg003_heads.json, which learned to read the head the scanner garbles worst: 146:0 is head (15) and 292:232 is head (28). The table's own ADNOTATIONES placement at 292:234 lands two characters later, inside a token, so it could not have been cut. The other two, 101:0 and 525:0, are not recoverable from the text OCR: head (9) is broken across two chunks and the number on the head at 525 is cut off at the scan edge. Both were instead read off the scan's own page layout, which carries a bounding box per word (data/pg003_head_geometry.json, and locus = leaf + 8, fitted on four independent column numbers). Leaf 93 is locus 101: its page header changes from DE COELESTI HIERARCHIA, CAP. 1. - CORDERII NOTAE on the leaf before to PARAPHRASIS PACHYMERAE (9), and the Greek printed under it is the Της ιεραρχιας αυτης απασης our row 101 opens with. Leaf 517 is locus 525: the display head sits 68 percent down the page, but everything above it there is Latin, which our Greek rows do not carry, so the paraphrase is still the first thing in the row. Both fall at the first character of a page for that reason, not by assumption.
Two boundaries are not taken and the four blocks they separate stay in the volume file: our OCR spliced the head into the middle of the preceding word, so the offset is not at a whitespace boundary and this tool would refuse it. 283:1586 reads ...to a)su/gKEFALAION Z'. and 440:321 reads ...LaIOIIFi/KEFALAION Z'. That leaves EH cap. VII (2,907 tokens), DN cap. VII (1,485) and their two paraphrase blocks (2,382 and 1,272) uncarved, plus locus 568, whose 20 tokens are Maximus quoted inside a Latin note and belong to neither author.
Check: against the TLG canon word counts in data/cgpg_works.json each work lands within 3 percent once its uncarved block is added back. CH 10,742 v 11,488 less the cap. I text absent from the dump; EH 13,074+2,907 v 16,400; DN 22,295+1,485 v 24,104; MT 1,313 v 1,350; Epistulae 6,569 v 6,668.

works.title: De caelesti hierarchia
works.evidence: Fifteen blocks, loci 71-192, each opened by its KEFALAION head; ours kept it at 89:1552, 107:865, 110:178, 136:0, 143:1521, 168:0 and 171:0. The dump starts mid-paraphrase, so cap. I's own text (Migne cols 119-126) is absent and is not claimed. Cap. XV's printed title (170:1847 to end of row) stays with the paraphrase: its head sits 128 words from the nearest anchor and the table declines it.

works.title: Epistulae
works.evidence: Loci 540-567 entire, ten epistles with no paraphrase between them. 540:0 opens Ep. 1 (To sko/tos a)fane\s gi/netai tw=| fwti/) on the row after the Mystical Theology paraphrase ends; 567 closes Ep. 10. Locus 568 is excluded on purpose: its 20 tokens are Maximus quoted inside a Latin note.

works.title: Paraphrasis in omnia opera Dionysii Areopagitae
works.evidence: Forty blocks opened by a PARAPHRASIS PACHYMERAE head, from (1) at the first row of the dump to (60) at 536. Our own OCR kept the head as garbled Latin at 151:0, 381:0 and 487:0; the rest come from the aligned table, four from the same witness but not from the table (101, 146, 292, 525; see basis). Two blocks are missing, the ones facing the two heads that cannot be cut at a whitespace boundary.
